Check yeast activity, proofing temperature, ingredient proportions, and whether the recipe would normally rise slowly. Don’t assume that two hours means the dough has failed. Give me practical checks in priority order, explain what each result suggests, and recommend whether to wait, adjust conditions, or start over.

My API sometimes returns yesterday’s data after an update. Please trace the cache invalidation path and fix the stale responses. Start with a reproducible example of an update followed by a stale read. Follow the write, transaction completion, cache keys, invalidation or refresh, and subsequent read across whichever cache layers actually exist. Check for timing races, inconsistent keys, and differences between application instances without assuming the cache is the only cause. Establish the intended freshness behavior from the existing contracts. Make a focused fix, add regression coverage for the stale-response scenario, and run the relevant tests. Report the root cause, verification results, and any remaining limitations.

I keep getting “permission denied” when running my shell script. Help me determine whether the problem is file permissions or something else. Ask for my operating environment, exact command, full error message, and relevant permissions if needed. Distinguish a failure to launch the script from a command inside it failing. Check executable permissions, access to parent directories, the interpreter and shebang, filesystem execution restrictions, and any files the script accesses where relevant. Explain the evidence for each diagnosis and recommend the narrowest fix. Avoid broad permission changes or elevated privileges as a default, and confirm the original command works afterward.

My calendar reminders have been arriving an hour late since I traveled. Help me untangle the time zone settings and restore reminders to the intended time. Ask which calendar app and devices I use, my previous and current time zones, and one affected event’s scheduled time and actual reminder time. Compare the device, calendar account, event, and reminder settings, including automatic time zone detection and daylight saving time where relevant. Check whether the event itself shifted or only the notification arrived late. Explain the likely mismatch before recommending changes, preserve existing event times unless a correction is needed, and verify the result with a test reminder.

I want to fix a mobile menu that opens correctly but won’t close when I tap outside it or press Escape. Check the menu implementation, its event handlers, and any relevant tests to identify the root cause before changing anything. Follow the project’s existing patterns and make the smallest reliable fix. Both outside taps and Escape should close the menu, while interactions inside it should still work normally. Check for event propagation issues, listener cleanup, and focus handling where relevant. Verify opening and both closing behaviors, and explain what changed and how you tested it. If the code isn’t available, ask for the relevant files.

My GitHub Actions build started failing after a dependency update. I want you to identify the breaking change and suggest the smallest reliable fix. Compare the failing build output with the dependency changes, lockfile, workflow configuration, and last successful build where available. Check whether the problem comes from the updated dependency, a transitive dependency, or a compatibility requirement, and distinguish confirmed findings from hypotheses. Recommend a focused fix, explain why it addresses the failure, and describe how to validate it. Avoid unrelated upgrades or refactoring. If you’re missing evidence, ask for the specific logs or diff you need.

I’ve got eggs, rice, and frozen peas. What can I make for dinner using those ingredients? Suggest one simple meal with approximate quantities for one person and clear, short cooking steps. Assume I have basic salt, pepper, and cooking oil, but label any other additions as optional. Cover both cooked rice and uncooked rice so I can follow the instructions either way. Include the approximate cooking time and keep the recipe practical, with minimal equipment and washing up.

Help me decode this laundry label: wash at 30°C, no tumble drying, cool iron. Explain each instruction in plain language and turn it into a short, practical sequence for washing, drying, and ironing the item. Tell me what temperature settings to look for and what to avoid. Don’t assume a particular fabric or add care instructions that aren’t supported by the label. If drying position or another detail depends on missing symbols, make that uncertainty clear.

I’m spending two nights at a friend’s place. Make me a small packing list that covers the essentials without overpacking. Assume it’s a casual visit with no special activities planned, and that I’ll wear one outfit when I travel. Include clothes, sleepwear, toiletries, my phone charger, and any personal medication I normally need. Group the list so it’s easy to check off, and keep weather-dependent or optional items separate. Aim for everything to fit in one small bag.

I need a polite text asking my upstairs neighbor to keep the music down after 10. Assume I mean 10 p.m. Write one short, natural message I can send as-is. Keep it friendly and clear about the time and the request, without sounding accusatory, overly apologetic, or formal. Don’t invent a history of noise problems or personal reasons I haven’t given. I want to preserve a good relationship while making the request easy to understand.

I’ve got $80 for groceries this week for one person. Help me plan simple meals for seven days, covering breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Assume I have no dietary restrictions and only basic oil, salt, and pepper at home; state those assumptions. Reuse ingredients and leftovers to keep cooking manageable and reduce waste. Give me a compact meal plan and a shopping list with quantities, approximate prices, and a total within $80, leaving a little room for price differences. Treat prices as estimates because I haven’t specified my location, and include easy substitutions if something costs more.

My kitchen’s a mess and I’ve got 15 minutes. Where do I start? Give me a realistic, timed cleanup plan that tells me exactly what to do first and what to tackle next. Assume I have ordinary cleaning supplies. Prioritize obvious rubbish, food that needs putting away, dishes, and usable counter space. Keep each step short and avoid deep cleaning or reorganizing cupboards. Allocate the full 15 minutes and tell me what I can leave for later so I finish with a noticeably more usable kitchen.

Make me a grocery list for spaghetti with tomato sauce and a green salad for four people. Assume a simple meat-free sauce and a basic salad with an easy dressing, with ordinary dinner-sized portions. Group the list by grocery-store section and include practical quantities for each ingredient. List pantry staples separately so I can check what I already have. Keep optional extras clearly marked, and avoid specialty ingredients or unnecessary purchases.

I always forget what's in my fridge. Suggest a simple way for me to track food and use it before it goes bad. Assume I want something inexpensive that takes only a few minutes to maintain and doesn't require recording every item. Give me one practical system, explain how to set it up, and show a short example. Include an easy reminder habit and a way to prioritize leftovers and opened food without treating freshness estimates as safety guarantees.

I need a birthday gift under $25 for my brother, who likes cooking and hiking. Suggest five thoughtful, practical options, with a brief explanation of why each fits his interests and an approximate price. Assume I don't know what equipment he already owns, so favor gifts that are useful even if he has the basics. Keep the total budget in mind, including likely shipping or tax, and recommend your strongest choice without inventing current prices or availability.

Help me write a return request for shoes that arrived in the wrong size. I want a short, polite but firm message I can send to the seller. Explain the problem and ask for return instructions and a prepaid return label. Assume I want a refund unless I specify otherwise. Use placeholders for the order number, size ordered, size received, and delivery date. Don't invent purchase details, seller policies, or legal claims.

I keep rushing out the door. Build me a realistic morning routine that takes 30 minutes from getting up to leaving home. Assume I need to wash, get dressed, have a simple breakfast, and collect my essentials. Give me a timed schedule with a small buffer for delays, plus a short list of things to prepare the night before. Keep it manageable, and include a fallback for mornings when I start five minutes late.

I've got a navy blazer, black jeans, and white sneakers. Does that combination work for a casual dinner? Assume the restaurant has no formal dress code and the clothes are clean and fit well. Give me a clear verdict and explain briefly how the colors and level of formality work together. Suggest a shirt or top and one or two small styling adjustments using common wardrobe basics. Keep the advice practical without turning this into a shopping list.

I spilled coffee on my white cotton shirt. What should I do first? Assume the spill just happened and I have ordinary household supplies. Lead with the immediate action, then give me a short, ordered set of steps to reduce the stain without damaging the fabric. Explain what to avoid and when to check the care label. If coffee with milk or sugar needs different treatment, mention that briefly. Don't promise complete stain removal.

I'm choosing between a 20-minute bike ride and a 45-minute bus ride to work. Help me weigh the everyday tradeoffs, including time, cost, weather, reliability, safety, exercise, arriving sweaty, and carrying things. Assume these are one-way travel times, and distinguish travel time from preparation or waiting time. Use a compact comparison and give me a conditional recommendation based on different priorities. Don't invent local conditions or fares; identify which missing details would most affect the choice.

I've got guests arriving in an hour. Give me a quick, realistic cleaning checklist that prioritizes what they'll notice and use: the entrance, seating area, bathroom, and kitchen surfaces. Assume I'm cleaning on my own with basic supplies. Break the hour into short blocks, put the highest-impact jobs first, and leave a few minutes for getting myself ready. Tell me what I can skip and include a shorter fallback if I run behind. My goal is a welcoming, reasonably clean home, not a deep clean.

My houseplant's soil is still wet a week after watering. Help me figure out what to check before I change anything. I haven't specified the plant or its growing conditions, so ask for the few details that would most affect your advice. Give me an ordered checklist covering drainage, standing water, pot size, soil, light, temperature, and signs of root trouble. Explain how to check moisture below the surface and distinguish normal slow drying from a potential problem. Include sensible immediate steps without assuming wet soil alone means root rot.

I want a simple system for keeping track of bills without downloading another app. Assume I can use paper or a spreadsheet I already have; recommend one low-maintenance approach and briefly explain the alternative. Show me a copyable tracker with the essential fields, including bill name, amount, due date, payment method, and paid status. Include how to handle automatic payments, variable amounts, and less frequent bills. Give me a short weekly routine and an initial setup checklist. I want to see what's due and confirm what's paid without maintaining a complicated budget.

I'm too tired to attend dinner tonight. Help me cancel kindly without making up an excuse. Write a short, natural message I can send that honestly says I don't have the energy, acknowledges the late notice, and shows appreciation for the invitation. Since I haven't said who invited me, give me a casual version for a friend and a slightly more considerate version for someone hosting. Avoid overexplaining or sounding dramatic, and make any offer to reschedule optional so I don't promise something I can't follow through on.

I can't find my wallet. Give me a systematic search plan that helps me avoid checking the same places repeatedly. Start with reconstructing when I last definitely had it, then work through likely places at home, clothing, bags, transport, and places I've visited. Use short, ordered steps and explain how to mark an area as fully checked. Include a sensible checkpoint for contacting places or moving from searching to protecting my cards if it may be lost outside. Don't assume it's stolen or tell me to cancel everything immediately.

I'm arranging a small living room. What should I measure before buying a sofa? Give me a practical checklist covering the room, usable wall space, doors and their swing, windows, radiators, existing furniture, and walking routes. Include the delivery route through entrances, hallways, stairs, or lifts, plus the sofa dimensions I need from the seller. Explain how to mark its footprint on the floor and account for reclining or convertible features if relevant. Distinguish useful clearance guidelines from measurements I must verify. I want to check both room fit and delivery access before buying.

I'm watching my friend's dog for the weekend. Give me a concise checklist of what to ask them before they leave. Prioritize feeding, walks, toilet routines, medication instructions, behavior, escape risks, and how long the dog can be left alone. Include emergency contacts, their vet's details, what to do if I can't reach them, and any permissions or arrangements for urgent care. Ask about supplies, sleeping arrangements, house rules, and interactions with other animals or people. Keep it easy to send to my friend or work through together, without assuming where the dog will stay.

Help me split household chores fairly with my roommate when our work schedules are different. I want a practical arrangement we can discuss and try, without assuming fairness means an equal number of tasks. Explain how to account for time, effort, frequency, preferences, and shared expectations about cleanliness, including planning and buying supplies. Give me a simple chore table we can adapt and a respectful conversation starter. Include how to handle busy weeks, missed tasks, and swaps, with a brief review after a trial period. Ask for our schedules and main chores before suggesting specific assignments.

My bedroom gets afternoon sun and feels stuffy at night. Suggest inexpensive, practical ways I can keep it cooler, prioritizing free changes before anything I need to buy. Assume I want to work with my existing room rather than install air conditioning or make permanent alterations. Explain when to block sunlight, open windows, and use a fan, accounting for whether the air outside is cooler. Give me a short plan to try tonight and a few affordable improvements if that isn't enough.

I want to organize my freezer so I actually use what's in it. Give me a simple system for sorting the food, making older items easy to find, and keeping track of what needs using soon. Assume I want to use containers and labels I already have before buying organizers. Include a manageable first organizing session, an easy inventory format, and a brief weekly habit that connects the contents to meal planning. Explain how to handle unidentified items without guessing whether they're safe.

I'm attending a wedding with a 'dressy casual' dress code, and I want to understand what I could wear without feeling underdressed or overly formal. Explain the usual meaning in plain language and give a few complete outfit options across different clothing preferences, including shoes and simple accessories. Don't assume my gender or that I need to buy a new outfit. Flag how the venue, weather, time of day, and any couple-specific instructions could change the choices, and mention common wedding etiquette pitfalls.

I struggle to let go of sentimental stuff, and I want a gentle way to sort just one box. Help me make progress without pressuring me to discard things or tackle my whole home. Suggest a short session with a few simple categories, compassionate questions for deciding what matters, and a way to handle items I'm unsure about. Include options for preserving memories while reducing physical clutter. Define success as making a few thoughtful decisions, and give me permission to pause if the process feels overwhelming.

I'm renting a car for three days and comparing two offers: $45 daily plus $20 daily insurance, or $62 daily with insurance included. Which costs less? Show the daily total and the full three-day total for each option, then state the difference and the cheaper choice clearly. Assume both offers cover the same three rental days and have equivalent insurance, with no other differing fees or taxes. Briefly note what I'd need to check if those assumptions don't hold.

I want to plan a low-key picnic date for under $30. Assume it's for two people, in a free nearby outdoor spot, and that I already have a blanket and basic reusable dishes. Give me one easy plan with a simple menu, drinks, a relaxed activity, and an itemized estimated budget that leaves a little room for price differences. Keep preparation and carrying things manageable. Include a short packing checklist and a weather backup. Treat the $30 as the total spending limit and state any excluded costs.

I need five work lunches that don't require a microwave. Suggest meals that taste good cold or at room temperature, are reasonably affordable, and can be packed without much morning effort. Assume I have no dietary restrictions and can use a refrigerator or an insulated bag with ice packs; make those storage assumptions explicit. For each lunch, list the main ingredients and brief preparation instructions. Include a combined shopping list and a simple advance-prep plan that reuses ingredients while keeping the five lunches varied.

My phone keeps distracting me in the evenings. Help me set a few manageable boundaries that let me relax and be more present without giving up my phone entirely. Assume I still need to receive important calls and messages. Suggest three small boundaries with clear times or triggers, an easy replacement activity for each, and a way to handle exceptions without abandoning the plan. Give me a one-week trial and a simple way to judge whether it's helping, using a supportive tone rather than guilt or strict productivity rules.

My train is delayed by 25 minutes. Write a short message I can send my friend letting them know I'll be late. Assume we're meeting soon and use a casual, friendly tone, with a brief apology. Mention the train delay without inventing an arrival time or other details. Keep it to one or two sentences and return just the message, ready to copy and send.

Help me make a bedtime routine I can stick to, even when I'm tired. My priority is something easy and repeatable. Assume I want a short routine that fits around my existing bedtime; don't invent a sleep schedule for me. Give me a normal version lasting about 15–20 minutes and a bare-minimum version for exhausted nights. Include a clear cue to start, a few steps in order, and an easy way to restart after missing a night.

I keep getting streaks when I clean my bathroom mirror. Help me figure out what to change in my cleaning method. Assume it's a standard bathroom mirror and that I'd prefer to use supplies I already have. Explain the likely causes, then give me a simple cleaning and drying sequence to try next time. Include how much cleaner to use, what kind of cloth works well, and whether humidity matters. Start with the easiest changes.

I need a warmer edit of my portrait, with natural skin tones and less glare on my glasses. Use my original photo as the starting point; if it isn't attached, ask me to provide it. Keep my facial features, skin texture, and overall appearance recognizable. Add subtle warmth without making my skin look orange, and reduce the reflections while preserving the glasses and any visible eye detail. Keep the original crop and resolution where possible. The finished portrait should look natural and gently improved.

Can you make me a spooky lighthouse illustration for a book cover, leaving room at the top for the title? Assume a vertical cover layout unless I provide dimensions. Make the lighthouse the main focal point, with an eerie atmosphere conveyed through lighting, mist, and the surrounding landscape. Keep the upper area uncluttered and suitable for readable title text. Don't add lettering or invent a book title. I'd like a finished illustration with a clear composition that still works at thumbnail size; leave exact print sizing open until I provide the cover specifications.

I want the background removed from my product photo and the result saved as a transparent PNG. Use the photo I provide; if it isn't attached, ask me for it. Preserve the entire product, including its colors, texture, labels, and fine edges. Remove the background cleanly without leaving halos, stray pixels, or cutting into the product. Keep the original resolution and framing where possible, and don't add a replacement background. Deliver a downloadable PNG with actual transparency, ready for me to use.

Help me understand why my phone videos look grainy indoors and what I can change to improve them. Explain the relationship between available light, the phone's camera sensor, and video settings in plain language. I haven't specified my phone model, so keep the initial advice general and flag anything that depends on the device. Give me a short, prioritized list of changes I can try with my current phone, starting with lighting, plus a simple comparison test to identify what helps most.

I'd like a practical shot list for a 30-second video introducing my neighborhood bakery. Assume a welcoming tone and that I'm filming on a phone with a small setup. Plan shots that introduce the location, show the baked goods and everyday activity, and end with a clear invitation to visit. Present a table with each shot's duration, subject, framing or movement, and suggested on-screen text or audio. Make the durations total exactly 30 seconds. Use placeholders for the bakery's name and details, and flag any shots that need staff or customer permission.

I need accurate captions for my interview recording, delivered as an SRT file with speaker labels and timestamps. Transcribe the speech faithfully, including meaningful spoken details, and keep captions readable with sensible line breaks and timing. Use consistent labels such as Interviewer and Guest when roles are clear; otherwise use Speaker 1 and Speaker 2. Do not guess names or unclear words. Flag uncertain passages for review separately. Check that timestamps match the recording, entries are numbered correctly, and captions do not overlap. If the recording is missing, ask me to provide it.

I want a mellow instrumental loop for my cooking videos, featuring acoustic guitar and no vocals. Assume a 20–30-second loop unless I specify another length. Keep the arrangement warm, relaxed, and unobtrusive so it can sit comfortably beneath cooking sounds or narration. Use a gentle, steady rhythm and avoid dramatic changes or distracting accents. Deliver an audio file that repeats smoothly, without an audible gap, click, or abrupt musical change at the loop point. Include its duration and tempo, and make any usage restrictions clear without assuming rights you cannot verify.

My podcast audio has a steady hum. Help me remove it in Audacity while keeping the voices full and natural. Assume I am a beginner and give me a clear, ordered workflow, starting with saving an untouched copy. Explain how to identify the hum and choose appropriate filtering or noise reduction, with conservative starting settings and guidance for adjusting them by ear. Avoid assuming the hum frequency without checking it. Include a short before-and-after listening check for thin voices, muffled speech, or processing artifacts, and explain when to back off the treatment.

I need concise alt text for my chart comparing monthly rainfall in three cities. Read the chart and preserve its main trend, the most important differences between cities, and any notable exceptions. Use the city names and units shown, but include individual values only when they are essential to understanding the pattern. Aim for one or two clear sentences rather than describing every point or visual styling. Do not invent unreadable data. If the chart is missing or unclear, ask for the chart or its underlying data before writing the final alt text.

Give me exactly three funny captions for my photo of a cat sitting inside a mixing bowl. Keep each caption short, punchy, and ready to post. Assume I want lighthearted, family-friendly humor, with a different joke or angle in each option rather than three variations of the same line. Base the jokes on the cat and mixing bowl; do not invent other visible details. Return only the three captions, with no explanation or hashtags.

I want my vacation clips turned into a one-minute montage, with gentle transitions and the original ocean sounds clearly audible. Assume the montage should keep the source clips’ predominant orientation and use no added music unless I request it. Choose the strongest moments and arrange them into a relaxed, cohesive sequence, trimming repetitive or shaky footage where practical. Keep transitions subtle and smooth the audio between clips without drowning out the waves. Deliver the finished 60-second video as an MP4. If the clips are missing, ask me to provide them.

Can you explain aperture to me using simple examples? Assume I am new to photography. Explain what aperture is, how f-stop numbers relate to the size of the opening, and how aperture affects brightness and how much of a scene looks sharp. Use everyday examples, such as a portrait with a blurry background and a landscape with more detail in focus. When comparing brightness, make clear that the other exposure settings are held constant. Keep the explanation approachable and finish with a short practical exercise I can try.

I'd like you to compare my two logo drafts for legibility at small sizes and explain which would work better on packaging. Examine the lettering, spacing, contrast, distinctive shapes, and details that may disappear when reduced or printed. Assume ordinary printed packaging unless I provide a specific material or process, and state where that assumption affects your recommendation. Give me a clear choice, explain the trade-offs, and suggest a few targeted improvements to the stronger draft. Base the assessment on the actual designs; if they are missing, ask me to provide both.

I recorded a voiceover too quickly. Please edit the recording I provide to slow it down slightly while keeping my pitch and vocal tone natural, and trim the long silence at the beginning. Assume a modest speed reduction of about 5–10%, adjusting within that range for comfortable pacing. Preserve natural pauses and avoid audible distortion. Return the edited audio in its original format, keep the source intact, and briefly note the changes.

I need a quick birthday text for my brother that’s funny but not sappy. Write a ready-to-send message in one or two short sentences, with a casual sibling tone and a light joke. Assume affectionate teasing is welcome, but avoid anything mean or overly sentimental. Don’t invent his age, interests, or shared memories. Give me three options so I can choose the one that sounds most like me.

Help me write an email declining a job offer while leaving the door open for future opportunities. I want to sound appreciative, professional, and clear about my decision without overexplaining. Thank them for the offer and their time, decline politely, and express interest in staying in touch. Don’t invent a reason for declining or imply I might accept this offer later. Include a subject line and use placeholders for names, the role, and the company.

I want this sentence to sound less defensive: “As I already explained, the delay wasn't my fault.” Help me communicate that I wasn’t responsible for the delay without sounding irritated, accusatory, or dismissive. Assume this is for a professional conversation. Preserve the meaning without adding an apology or accepting responsibility I haven’t stated. Give me three concise alternatives, ranging from neutral to more collaborative, and identify the best general-purpose option.

I’m announcing that my bakery will close on Mondays starting next month. Draft a friendly Instagram caption that clearly explains the change and thanks customers for understanding. Keep it warm, welcoming, and brief, with the new Monday closure easy to spot. Don’t invent a reason, other opening hours, or a reopening date. Use [month] as a placeholder rather than guessing the timing. Give me one ready-to-post caption with light, optional emoji use.

I need a formal letter asking my landlord to repair the leaking bedroom ceiling, which I reported two weeks ago. Make it polite but firm: reference my earlier report, explain that the issue remains unresolved, and request prompt repairs plus written confirmation of the proposed schedule. Don’t invent damage, health effects, legal obligations, or previous promises. Use placeholders for names, the property address, dates, and contact details. Return a complete letter I can personalize and send.

I’m giving a two-minute wedding toast for my best friend. We met on a disastrous camping trip, and I want that to be the opening anecdote. Write a toast that’s warm, lightly funny, and suitable for her grandparents, with affectionate humor and a sincere closing toast to the couple. Aim for roughly 240–270 words so I have room for pauses and laughter. Don’t invent camping mishaps, names, or details about their relationship; use a few clear placeholders where personal details are needed. Make it sound natural when spoken, with an easy transition from our chaotic first meeting to our friendship and my wishes for their marriage.

I need a subject line for an overdue invoice reminder. Assume this is a professional reminder to a customer, and keep the tone polite, clear, and firm without sounding threatening. Make the purpose immediately recognizable and keep each option short enough to scan easily in an inbox. Don’t invent an invoice number, amount, or deadline; use a placeholder if needed. Give me five options and recommend one for a first reminder.

Help me write a short, sincere apology to a friend after I canceled dinner twice. I want to acknowledge the inconvenience and take responsibility without making excuses, sounding overly dramatic, or asking them to reassure me. Assume this is a casual text message and keep the language warm and natural. Don’t invent a reason for the cancellations or promise a new date. Give me one ready-to-send version that leaves room for my friend’s feelings.

Help me clarify this sentence: ‘Employees may not submit requests after Friday unless approval has not yet been received.’ Give me clear versions for both possible meanings: employees can submit after Friday if approval is still pending, or employees can submit after Friday only if approval has already been received. Label each version by its meaning and briefly explain the difference. Preserve the reference to Friday without inventing a deadline time or approval process, and flag that the second interpretation changes the original sentence’s literal condition.

Write a 150-word author bio for my first poetry collection. I’m a former nurse from Leeds, and my poems explore grief, ordinary routines, and coastal landscapes. Assume the bio will appear in the book and use third person, with a warm, understated literary tone. Use [Name] as a placeholder for my name and avoid assuming my pronouns. Don’t invent publications, awards, qualifications, personal losses, or connections between my nursing career and my poetry. Make the supplied details feel cohesive without overstating them, and ensure the finished bio is exactly 150 words.

Write a short fundraising appeal for our community garden. We’re raising £800 to cover accessible raised beds and tools, and I want a clear, friendly invitation to donate. Assume this will be shared with local residents in a community post or email. Explain what their donations will help provide, keep the tone welcoming and practical, and avoid guilt or exaggerated promises. Use [donation link] as a placeholder, and don’t invent a deadline, charity status, or details about the garden. Give me one ready-to-use appeal.

Help me find a polite way to say ‘please stop replying all’ in a group email thread. I want the request to be clear without embarrassing anyone or sounding irritated or patronizing. Assume a professional setting, and suggest replying directly to me when the response doesn’t concern the whole group. Give me three brief, ready-to-send options: one gentle, one neutral, and one slightly firmer. Keep each option to one or two sentences and avoid implying that relevant group replies are unwelcome.

Draft a plain-language customer email based on this technical update: our database migration is complete, average page loads are 20% faster, and no action is required. I want customers to understand the benefit without needing technical knowledge. Include a clear subject line and a brief, reassuring body. Explain the migration simply, preserve ‘average’ so the speed improvement isn’t presented as a guarantee for every page, and make the no-action message explicit. Don’t invent downtime, security improvements, or other benefits. Assume a friendly, professional tone.

Write a compassionate rejection note for a volunteer applicant whose availability doesn’t match our weekend shifts. Thank them for their interest and willingness to help, explain the scheduling mismatch clearly, and invite them to apply again if their schedule changes. Assume this is a short email and use placeholders for their name and our organization. Keep the tone warm and respectful without suggesting they lack ability or commitment. Don’t promise a future position or invent alternative opportunities. Include a simple subject line and a ready-to-send message.

Help me plan my week without cramming every hour. I want a realistic plan that makes room for important work, existing commitments, rest, and unexpected things. Start by asking a few focused questions about my priorities, fixed appointments, available time, and energy patterns. Then create a flexible weekly outline with a small number of priorities each day, generous buffer time, and clearly optional tasks. Assume I prefer broad blocks over an hour-by-hour schedule. Include a simple way to adjust the plan if something takes longer or my priorities change.

I have a proposal due Friday, overdue invoices, and six unread client emails. Help me decide what to tackle first today and turn that decision into a realistic action plan. Consider deadlines, financial impact, client relationships, and whether the emails could contain something that changes my priorities. Don't assume whether the invoices are bills I owe or payments clients owe me; explain how that affects the order. Give me a provisional ranked list, a concrete first action, and suggested time limits. Flag any missing information that could materially change your recommendation.

I keep forgetting monthly admin tasks. Make me a simple recurring checklist covering bills, expense reports, backups, and appointment booking. Organize it around one monthly admin session, with separate reminders for anything that has an earlier deadline. For each item, include what to check, the next action, and a clear definition of done. Assume I want a lightweight routine I can copy into a calendar or task list. Leave placeholders for my actual due dates, and don't assume that a monthly backup is sufficient for all my data.

My meetings run from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. tomorrow. Help me fit in two hours of writing, lunch, and a school pickup at 4:30 p.m. Treat the meetings and pickup as fixed commitments, and show me a schedule with explicit start and end times. If you need to assume a start time or travel time, state that assumption clearly. Protect focused writing time and allow a realistic buffer before pickup. If lunch cannot fit without a meeting break, flag the conflict and tell me what adjustment I need to make.

I need a simple Friday review routine that takes no more than 15 minutes. Create a repeatable, timeboxed checklist that helps me notice what I finished, catch loose ends, and choose my priorities for next week. Include a quick check of upcoming deadlines and commitments without turning this into a full planning session. Give each step a time allowance, keep the total within 15 minutes, and provide a short template I can reuse. Assume I want something practical enough to follow even when I'm tired or busy.

I'm drowning in little tasks. Help me set clear rules for deciding what to do now, batch, delegate, or drop. I want a lightweight decision process I can apply quickly to a messy task list. Consider urgency, consequences, effort, dependencies, and whether someone else can reasonably handle the task. Don't assume I have staff or that every short task deserves immediate attention. Give me concrete thresholds, a few examples, and a short checklist for sorting my backlog. Include a rule that prevents small tasks from consuming time reserved for important work.

Please draft a daily schedule for me as a freelancer working 9–5, with mornings reserved for client work and afternoons for sales and administration. Assume a typical weekday and include lunch, short breaks, and a little buffer for unexpected requests. Give me a timetable with clear start and end times and a purpose for each block. Keep morning client work protected, and make the afternoon split between sales and administration explicit. Include a simple rule for adjusting the schedule when client deadlines or meetings disrupt the day.

I want to stop checking email constantly. Suggest three daily email windows and a practical way to handle genuinely urgent messages between them. Assume a standard workday unless I give you different hours, and state that assumption. Specify the timing and duration of each window, what I should do during it, and when to stop. Define what counts as genuinely urgent, suggest an agreed alternative contact route, and give me a short message I can share with clients or colleagues. Make the routine realistic without requiring constant inbox monitoring.

My partner and I alternate grocery shopping and cleaning each week. Create a four-week rotation starting with me doing groceries in week one. Assume we each take one responsibility per week, so my partner handles cleaning in week one and we swap roles the following week. Show the rotation in a simple table labeled Week 1 through Week 4; I haven't supplied a calendar start date. Add a brief rule for repeating the pattern after week four and handling a temporary swap while keeping the workload balanced.

I have eight hours left this week and need a realistic plan: a report that will take four hours is due Thursday, I need three hours of interview prep for Friday, and I have two hours of optional filing. Help me prioritize and schedule the work around those deadlines. Since everything totals nine hours, explicitly show what to defer or reduce rather than squeezing it all in. Assume the report and interview prep take priority. Give me a simple time-block plan, explain any assumptions about my availability, and show how much time remains for filing or buffer.

I want a simple app for tracking books I’ve read. Help me turn that into a small, usable first version. Assume it’s for personal use, with book title, author, date finished, and optional rating or notes. I should be able to add, edit, delete, and browse entries, and keep my records after closing the app. Keep the interface straightforward and avoid expanding into social features or reading recommendations. Check any existing project context before choosing an implementation. Deliver a working version with brief setup instructions, and verify that the basic tracking flow works.

Help me build a shared grocery list where my housemates can add items, mark them bought, and see who changed what. Assume we need one household list that works well on phones. Keep the first version focused on adding items, checking them off, and a readable history showing who made each change and when. Make each housemate identifiable without assuming we need an elaborate account system. Changes should persist and become visible to everyone, and simultaneous edits should not silently overwrite each other. Check the existing project context, explain key assumptions, and deliver a working version with setup instructions and verification of the shared-list flow.

I’m making a habit tracker and want encouraging reminder messages that don’t sound judgmental when I miss a day. Write a small set of concise messages for a missed day, a few missed days, and returning after a longer break. Assume these appear as notifications or short in-app reminders. Keep the tone warm, natural, and supportive of my users’ choices. Avoid guilt, pressure about streaks, exaggerated praise, or assumptions about why someone missed their habit. Offer a gentle next step where appropriate. Give me three alternatives for each situation, clearly labeled, so I can choose a consistent voice.

I need a small web app for splitting trip expenses among friends, including costs shared by only some people. Assume one currency per trip and equal splits among the selected participants for each expense. I should be able to add friends, record an amount and payer, select who shared the cost, edit or remove expenses, and see everyone’s net balance and suggested repayments. Keep the interface simple and make the calculations understandable. Handle currency rounding consistently and ensure balances reconcile to zero. Check the existing project context before choosing an implementation. Deliver a working app with persistent records, setup instructions, and verified examples covering whole-group and partial-group expenses.

My recipe app feels cluttered. Help me decide what belongs on the home screen and what can move into a menu. Start by checking the current screens and features if they’re available; otherwise, ask me for a brief description and label any provisional assumptions. Assume the home screen should help people quickly find a recipe and start cooking. Recommend a clear information hierarchy, explain the placement of each major feature, and identify anything that could be combined or removed. Give me a concise home-screen layout and menu structure, with reasons tied to common user tasks rather than visual preference alone.

I wanna track my plants and watering dates. Help me make a simple app where I can add a plant, record when I water it, and see its latest watering date and history. Assume it’s just for me, and keep the first version easy to use on my phone. Let me edit plant details and correct a watering entry, and make sure my records stay saved. If you include watering intervals, let me set them for each plant instead of assuming a universal schedule.
